founded_place_size: Started 2020 in Portland, Oregon. A two-person operation with a mid six-figure subscriber base, publishing several times a week.
about: Voltcast is an independent consumer-tech review channel run by two people out of Portland. We buy or borrow the gear, run it hard, and say what we actually think. Episodes go out long-form to the main feed plus vertical and square shorts. About a third of the revenue is sponsor money, so the grid has to look like one channel and the sponsor read has to be exactly right.
audience: Enthusiast buyers and everyday shoppers who want an honest verdict before they spend. They follow us because we are not the manufacturer, and they can tell the difference.
price_positioning: Mid-tier creator economy. A sponsor integration is worth a few thousand dollars and renewal depends on how the segment looks. The channel has to read as a credible independent reviewer, never as broadcast gloss and never as raw phone-shot filler.

palette.name: Volt Orange
palette.usage: The verdict word on both films, set on Card Charcoal (type system step 01), plus thin accent rules and small highlights, as the rule along the top of the spec card in voltcast_e42_select_09.jpg; apart from the verdict word and the cover's optional ground, no more than 5% of the designed, non-photographic area. Never body text or a panel, and never a ground on either film; on the cover it may be one solid ground behind the photograph.

palette.name: Card Charcoal
palette.usage: The solid ground behind the verdict on both films (signature move) and the main ground or panel behind other type, as the spec card in voltcast_e42_select_09.jpg. The type colour on any Panel White panel and on the cover's optional Volt Orange ground.

palette.name: Bench Grey
palette.usage: Secondary solid panels and hairline dividers on Card Charcoal grounds. Never the verdict, never an accent.

palette.name: Panel White
palette.role: mandatory where type other than the verdict sits on Card Charcoal or Bench Grey
palette.usage: Unit names, the episode label, body text and figures on Card Charcoal or Bench Grey, as the column heads and figures in voltcast_e42_select_09.jpg. May also be a light solid panel, with Card Charcoal type on it. Never the verdict.

palette.name: Muted Steel
palette.usage: Secondary labels and units on Card Charcoal, as the units beside the figures in voltcast_e42_select_09.jpg, and hairline dividers. Never a ground, a panel or the verdict.

typography: Voltcast runs a grotesk over Inter, in four steps. Step 01, display, is the verdict in PP Radio Grotesk Bold at 96 px on 101 px leading on the 1080 square, tracking -15 units, one word only, all caps, Volt Orange on Card Charcoal, optically scaled until it touches both card margins at four times the body size, and 120 px on the vertical. Step 02, the subheading, is the episode label in PP Radio Grotesk Medium at 40 px on 46 px leading, tracked 80 units, all caps. Step 03, body, is Inter Regular at 30 px on 42 px leading, tracking 0, for body and sponsor copy held to 65 characters a line, with spec figures stepping up to Inter Medium tabular at 34 px and the print sheet at 9 pt. Step 04, fine print, is the disclosure in Inter Regular at 24 px on 34 px leading, tracking +10 units, which is the floor of the system and never goes smaller. The verdict never runs to two words.
voice: Direct, dry, and unhyped. We talk like a person who has actually used the thing. Sponsor copy runs as written and the disclosure line is exact. We never oversell.
brand_assets_status: The channel bug exists only as a flat export on white and we have no editable brand kit. On-screen cards get rebuilt from scratch every episode, which is the problem we want solved. We need the bug prepared as reusable artwork and the card set delivered as a file we can reopen and change each week.
values: Independence from the manufacturers we cover, honesty about what we tested, consistency across the grid, and respect for the audience that trusts the verdict.

rules: Never let the verdict run to two words.
The verdict is always all caps, tracked -15 units, and optically scaled until it touches both card margins, Volt Orange on Card Charcoal: 96 px on the 1080 square, 120 px on the vertical.

palette_rules.distribution: Grounds and panels are Card Charcoal, with Bench Grey for secondary panels and Panel White for any light panel; Muted Steel is never a ground or panel. Volt Orange is never a ground or panel on either film; on the cover it may be one solid ground behind the photograph, and is otherwise never a ground or panel there either. The verdict is Volt Orange on a solid Card Charcoal ground on both films. On Card Charcoal or Bench Grey, all other type is Panel White, with Muted Steel for secondary labels and units, as on voltcast_e42_select_09.jpg. On Panel White, and on the cover's optional Volt Orange ground, type is Card Charcoal. Volt Orange is the only accent: apart from the verdict word and the cover's optional ground, it appears only as thin accent rules and small highlights, together no more than 5% of the designed, non-photographic area.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity, on every held frame. No tint, transparency, gradient, shadow, glow or blend mode is applied to any palette colour, any type or the channel bug, and no scrim, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over the footage or the cover photograph. A straight cut or a plain fade between two shots is a transition, not a tint.
palette_rules.forbidden: No colour outside the five palette hexes for type, grounds, panels, rules or icons; the one exception is the channel bug, placed in the ink of voltcast_bug_transparent.svg or voltcast_bug_reversed.svg as supplied. No second accent colour, no glow, drop shadow, bevel or other broadcast-gloss effect on any type, panel or the bug, and no Meridian VPN logo on any output in this pack.
palette_rules.photography: The supplied footage (voltcast_e42_master.mp4, voltcast_e42_bench_02.mp4, voltcast_e42_panel_03.mp4, voltcast_e42_load_04.mp4 and voltcast_e42_carry_05.mp4) and the cover photograph keep their own colour and are never tinted, duotoned or graded toward the palette; colours inside the picture, such as a unit's orange accent stripe, are not design colours.
